questions.prompt: Which of these is a right angle?
questions.explanation: A right angle is exactly 90°, like the corner of a book. 180° is a straight angle.

questions.prompt: An angle measures 130°. What kind of angle is it?
questions.explanation: 130° is bigger than 90° and smaller than 180°, so it is obtuse. Acute angles are smaller than 90°.

questions.prompt: You bisect an angle of 90°. How big is each part?
questions.explanation: Bisect means cut into two equal parts: 90 ÷ 2 = 45. Doubling gives 180, which is the opposite of bisecting.

questions.prompt: You bisect 60°, then you bisect one of the parts again. What angle do you get?
questions.explanation: 60 ÷ 2 = 30, then 30 ÷ 2 = 15. If you stop after one cut you only reach 30°.

questions.prompt: An angle was bisected. Each part is 35°. How big was the whole angle?
questions.explanation: Two equal parts make the whole: 35 + 35 = 70. Dividing 35 by 2 goes the wrong way.

questions.prompt: Where do you put the centre of the protractor?
options: At the end of the longer line
On the point where the two lines meet
questions.explanation: The centre sits on the meeting point, with the zero line along one side. Anywhere else gives a wrong reading.
